purpose: The real 2006 NBA Draft (June 28, 2006) as world data: picks, original owners and draft-night rights moves. Usable only from the draft date and never an input to the simulated lottery, draft order or picks; a real Miami pick or trade is skipped (AGENTS.md rule 1) and simulated Miami picks on its own.

location.value: The Theater at Madison Square Garden, New York City

total_picks.note: 30 first-round and 30 second-round picks (no forfeited pick)

winner.note: Toronto won from the fifth seed (8.8% chance)

charlotte.value: Charlotte took part in the 2006 lottery as an ordinary club (no fixed slot).

lottery.draft_order_status: Picks 1-14 by original owner, from the Wikipedia lottery table and the BBR draft table. Pick 2 is New York's slot (owned by Chicago from the October 4, 2005 Eddy Curry trade).

pre_lottery_odds_by_team.note: Only seed-level odds are rules (nba_2006_lottery_rules.json); club-by-club odds are real-season hindsight and not recorded.

post_draft_rights_moves_status: one recorded: Rudy Gay's rights (No. 8), Houston to Memphis, agreed on draft night and completed July 12, 2006; no other post-draft rights trade of a 2006 pick was found in the sources read; unverified as complete

miami_summary.value: Real Miami's 2006 first-round pick (No. 26, Jordan Farmar) had gone to the Lakers in the July 14, 2004 Shaquille O'Neal trade, and its second-round pick (No. 56) to Boston in the August 2005 five-team trade (then New Orleans/Oklahoma City and Toronto, which selected Edin Bavčić). Real Miami transactions are not applied (AGENTS.md rule 1): simulated Miami kept both picks until its own moves, and sent its 2006 first to the New Orleans/Oklahoma City Hornets on 2006-01-16 (career/Dwyane_Wade/2005-06/00_Team/Finances/draft_picks.json; nba_2006_pick_ownership.json).

notes: Several Wikipedia source rows mark later-career honors (*, #, +, ~); these were deliberately omitted.

Draft-night rights moves: 2 CHI->POR, 4 POR->CHI, 6 MIN->POR, 7 BOS->MIN (via POR), 13 PHI->CHI, 16 CHI->PHI, 21 PHO->BOS, 27 PHO->POR, 31 POR->IND, 37 MIN->PHI, 44 ORL->HOU, 45 IND->MEM (via POR), 49 DEN->BOS, 51 LAL->DET, 56 TOR->PHI, 58 DAL->LAL, 59 SAS->MIL.
Pick 8 (Rudy Gay): the Houston-Memphis trade was agreed on draft night and completed July 12, 2006, so Houston held the rights at the end of draft night (post_draft_rights_moves_not_draft_night).
Pick 20: Wikipedia's footnote s prints the Kenyon Martin trade as July 15, 2005; footnote q dates it July 15, 2004 (Kenyon Martin's move to Denver in the 2004 offseason), which is followed.
Pick 34: Wikipedia's footnote x prints the Charlotte-Clippers trade as July 14, 2005; Basketball-Reference and nba_2005_draft_class.json date it July 14, 2004, which is followed.

Pick 44: Wikipedia's footnote ab leaves the Milwaukee-Cleveland Jiří Welsch trade undated; the Bucks' 2005 Basketball-Reference transactions date it June 28, 2005, the day Cleveland passed the pick to Orlando.

Pick 49 (Leon Powe): the Wikipedia table lists him as a California junior; Sports-Reference and the NBA's June 19, 2006 list as a sophomore. The evidence file's college_class follows Sports-Reference.

Club codes are Basketball-Reference's 2005-06 codes (NOK for the New Orleans/Oklahoma City Hornets, SEA for Seattle). Positions and schools are from Wikipedia; BBR does not list positions on its draft page.
All bbr_ids are as linked from basketball-reference.com's 2006 draft page; none were guessed.
